title: MM-MT105-OrchestratorNotificationPath

scope.summary:
GOAL: Event-driven worker-to-orchestrator notification with ZERO polling. Worker completion, blocker, and signal events (from the MT-009 event bus plus MT-121 MT-signal contract) are delivered INTO the orchestrator session as steer-queue messages via MT-002, so the orchestrator model is woken by its children's outcomes instead of burning turns asking. Operator rule (governance memory): polling is a defect — this MT is the mechanical notification/callback path that removes it from model-to-model orchestration. This is also the async orchestrator-workers wiring Anthropic's research system lacks (their orchestrator blocks synchronously on workers).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New file src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/model_tools/notify_path.rs (subscriber + router + batcher + dedupe) wired at coordinator/service startup; notification message schema addition in model_tools/types.rs; delivery records in the ledger. Tests. No frontend changes.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Subscription: subscribe on the MT-009 event bus to child-session terminal events (completed/failed/cancelled — the FR-EVT-SWARM-SESSION-COMPLETED / -FAILED / -CANCELLED family in src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/events.rs), blocker events, and MT-121 structured MT-signals emitted by workers. Routing key: MT-103 lineage — each event routes to the live parent of the emitting child; events for children whose parent is terminated route nowhere but are recorded as undeliverable (no crash, no silent drop).
2. Delivery: notifications are wrapped as a typed `worker_notification` steer message (schema: notification_id, child_session_id, role_id, kind = `completed | failed | cancelled | blocker | signal`, signal payload ref, occurred_at, batch info) and enqueued onto the MT-002 steer queue addressed to the parent session — the SAME queue and turn-boundary semantics as any steer (capability-aware per transport via the MT-102 delivery classes). No new delivery transport is invented.
3. Content safety: worker-authored content inside a notification (final report body, blocker text, signal free-text) is passed through the MT-104 injection scan before enqueue; quarantined bodies deliver the notification envelope WITH the quarantine_id instead of the body (the orchestrator learns the child finished and that the report is quarantined — no silent loss, no unscanned delivery).
4. Batching + backpressure: a per-parent batching window (config, default 500ms) coalesces bursts into one steer message carrying up to N notifications (config, default 20); queue-depth backpressure defers batches when the parent's steer queue exceeds a config threshold rather than dropping. Deferral is bounded (max age config, default 60s) — past it, delivery is forced regardless of depth so notifications cannot age out invisibly.
5. Dedupe: notification_id is deterministic (child_session_id + event id) and an at-least-once bus is assumed; the router keeps a bounded seen-window per parent and drops exact duplicates, recording the drop as a dedupe (not a loss).
6. Delivery accounting: every notification's lifecycle (received-from-bus, batched, enqueued, deferred, forced, deduped, undeliverable) is ledgered; MT-108 asserts a completed worker produces exactly one delivered notification at the parent with a full ledger trail (HBR-SWARM-002 no-silent-loss).
7. Zero-polling proof obligation: no code path in this MT sleeps-and-checks or timer-scans session state to detect completion; the only timers permitted are the batching window and deferral bound. An executable grep-level proof plus test asserts no polling loop exists in the notify path.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read MT-009 bus subscribe API, MT-121 signal schema, MT-002 enqueue API, MT-103 lineage queries, events.rs terminal-event catalogue.
2. Define WorkerNotification + batch envelope types in model_tools/types.rs.
3. Implement notify_path.rs: subscriber task (spawned at service startup under the coordinator's shutdown CancellationToken), lineage routing, MT-104 scan integration, batcher with window + cap, backpressure deferral with bounded age, dedupe window.
4. Ledger every lifecycle transition.
5. Tests per expected_tests.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (except named IPC/GUI surfaces for the GUI MT; this MT names none)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/coordinator.rs (read-only; subscriber hooks the existing event seam and shutdown token only)
acceptance_criteria: Worker terminal events, blockers, and MT-121 signals reach the parent session as typed worker_notification steer messages via the MT-002 queue; no new transport is introduced.
Routing uses MT-103 lineage; notifications for children of terminated parents are recorded undeliverable — never crash, never silently dropped.
Worker-authored bodies are MT-104-scanned before enqueue; quarantined bodies deliver envelope + quarantine_id, never the raw body.
Batching coalesces bursts within the configured window/cap; backpressure defers (bounded by max age) and never drops; forced delivery past max age is ledgered as forced.
Exact duplicate bus events are deduped via deterministic notification_id with the drop recorded as dedupe.
Ledger trail covers every notification lifecycle state; a completed worker yields exactly one delivered notification at the parent (asserted end-to-end in MT-108).
Zero polling: no sleep-and-check or timer-scan of session state anywhere in the notify path; only the batching window and deferral bound timers exist (grep proof + code review criterion).
Subscriber shuts down cleanly under the coordinator shutdown CancellationToken (no orphan task after teardown).
expected_tests: integration: child completion event arrives at parent as one worker_notification steer message
integration: 25-event burst within window delivers as batched messages respecting cap 20
integration: backpressure defers then force-delivers past max age with ledger states deferred->forced
unit: deterministic notification_id and dedupe window drops exact duplicates only
integration: quarantined report body delivers envelope with quarantine_id
negative: parent terminated => undeliverable recorded, no panic
shutdown: cancellation token stops the subscriber task with no residue
implementation_notes: Operator governance rule baked in: polling is a defect. The orchestrator model never calls worker_status in a loop to detect completion; worker_status (MT-102) remains for on-demand inspection, this path is the push channel.
At-least-once bus assumption: dedupe is mandatory; if the MT-009 bus turns out exactly-once, dedupe stays as cheap insurance (documented).
The batch envelope keeps individual notification integrity: consumers can attribute each item to its child and ledger row even inside a batch.
Blocker notifications are how a stuck worker escalates without dying; pair with MT-121 signal kinds; escalation policy itself (what the orchestrator does) is model behavior, not this MT.
Cross-family seams (reference only): MT-002 steer queue, MT-009 event bus, MT-102 delivery classes, MT-103 lineage, MT-104 scan, MT-121 signal contract, MT-161 FR kinds.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless routing path; the live steering/notification feed becomes operator-visible in MT-107.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal push path with no new operator-facing controls; MT-107 documents the visible feed and MT-108 documents the end-to-end behavior.

risk_if_missed: Orchestrator models must poll children (operator-declared defect: token burn, latency, missed blockers) or workers complete into the void; blockers go unnoticed and the async-steering advantage over the Anthropic synchronous pattern is lost.

risks: RISK-1: Silent notification loss — a dropped bus event, race at parent termination, or backpressure drop means a worker completed but its orchestrator never learns, stalling the whole tree.
RISK-2: Notification flood — a failing worker emitting rapid signals (or many children at once) floods the parent's steer queue and drowns operator steers.
RISK-3: Injection via notification body — worker report/blocker text delivered unscanned becomes an injection channel into the orchestrator (the highest-value target).
RISK-4: Duplicate-delivery loops — at-least-once bus delivery double-notifies and a naive orchestrator double-acts (e.g. double spawn of a follow-up worker).
RISK-5: Covert polling reintroduction — the implementation 'simplifies' to a timer scan of session state, silently violating the operator's zero-polling rule.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Full lifecycle ledger accounting including undeliverable + forced states; bounded deferral (never indefinite); MT-108 asserts exactly-one-delivery with trail.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Per-parent batching window + cap and queue-depth backpressure with bounded deferral; burst test proves coalescing.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Mandatory MT-104 scan pre-enqueue; quarantine delivers envelope-only; dedicated test.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Deterministic notification_id + dedupe window; duplicate test proves single delivery.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Zero-polling acceptance criterion with executable grep proof target and code-review note; only batch-window/deferral timers permitted.

research_provenance.source: Direct source inspection 2026-07-21 of wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1: events.rs (SESSION-COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED FR events), coordinator.rs (shutdown CancellationToken ownership), process_ledger/ (accounting rows). Operator governance memory: polling is a defect; mechanical notification/callback required. External precedent: Anthropic multi-agent research system (synchronous-only steering named as their gap — this MT builds the async push they lack); event-driven callback patterns over at-least-once buses (dedupe + idempotency as standard hardening).
